decisions.reason: Particle-therapy water phantoms are closely related to the firm's dosimetry and QA knowledge base, but the narrower niche and the delayed, region-limited launch signal a higher-than-average risk of withdrawal if adoption stays modest.

A small-volume ionization chamber fits directly with the firm's established calibration, measurement, and clinical physics capabilities, so management is likely to retain and refine it rather than exit quickly.
This small-volume ionization chamber also builds strongly on existing chamber design and dosimetry know-how, giving the firm good capacity to learn from use and improve the product.
A standard clinical ionization chamber sits at the center of the firm's core competence and customer workflow, making continuation the most likely choice.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is highly complementary to the firm's QA portfolio and service model, so it is likely to stay unless it proves clearly redundant.
A thimble ionization chamber is a classic, closely related product for this business, and the firm's accumulated technical and calibration knowledge supports keeping it on the market.
